checks.title: Virtual machines without zone or availability set

waf.why: Redundancy across zones or sets limits the effect of one failure.

collector.violations: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.compute/virtualmachines' | where isnull(zones) or array_length(zones) == 0 | where isnull(properties.availabilitySet) | extend zoneCount = coalesce(array_length(zones), 0) | project id, name, subscriptionId, resourceGroup, location, zoneCount

checks.proves: The VM has no availability zone and is not in an availability set.
checks.doesNotProve: Whether the workload tolerates the loss of a zone, or whether more than one instance exists.

checks.title: Virtual machines without a backup item

waf.why: A backup item is one input of a recovery plan; it does not prove the plan, which is a practice.

collector.violations: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.compute/virtualmachines' | extend vmKey=tolower(id) | join kind=leftouter (recoveryservicesresources | where type =~ 'microsoft.recoveryservices/vaults/backupfabrics/protectioncontainers/protecteditems' | extend vmKey=tolower(tostring(properties.sourceResourceId)), hitR='y' | project vmKey, hitR) on vmKey | where isempty(hitR) | project id, name, subscriptionId, resourceGroup, location

checks.proves: No Azure Backup protected item names the VM as its source.
checks.doesNotProve: That a restore works, or that another backup product protects it. A protected item of another workload whose sourceResourceId is the VM counts as a backup of the VM (a false negative). If the right side of the join were cut by a limit that is not documented, VMs would be reported as unprotected for the wrong reason (not verified; manual test M-3).

checks.title: Resources reported as not available by Resource Health

waf.why: Health signals are part of measuring the solution's health.

collector.violations: healthresources | where type =~ 'microsoft.resourcehealth/availabilitystatuses' | where tostring(properties.availabilityState) !~ 'Available' | project id, subscriptionId, availabilityState=tostring(properties.availabilityState)

checks.proves: Resource Health reports an availability state other than Available.
checks.doesNotProve: The cause, the duration, or the application's own health.

checks.title: Recovery targets are defined

waf.why: Recovery and reliability targets are a design practice.

text.en: Are recovery time and recovery point targets defined for each workload, and approved by its owner?
text.pt-BR: Os objetivos de tempo e ponto de recuperação estão definidos para cada carga de trabalho e aprovados pelo responsável?

checks.proves: The answer of the person who knows the practice.
checks.doesNotProve: Whether the targets are met; no API shows it.
